prior_audit_preserved.finding: a1_evidence._norm_url (anchored) keeps leads whose host is not a DNS host (e.g. 'https://{x.com' -> 'https://{x.com/', 'https://ex ample.com', 'https://-x.com', underscore labels) and does not resolve dot segments ('/a/../b') or normalise percent-escapes ('%7E'), while the anchored text (amendment §9, decision-protocol.json E2) says 'absolute http(s) URLs with a DNS host only' and malformed values are dropped, and Freeze-1.1 URI rules require dot-segment resolution and unreserved decoding.
prior_audit_preserved.evidence: synthetic strings only (no A1 data), reproduced by test_registrations.D8Tests
prior_audit_preserved.precedence_consequence: the amendment states that if its text and machine files disagree it may not be used. This contradiction must therefore be resolved by a prospective amendment before the affected methodology is used.
prior_audit_preserved.impact: E2 starting links only (G4). Garbage leads fail to load and consume a page slot; duplicate un-normalised leads can consume two slots. No effect on G, primary entries, permutation, selection or estimand.
prior_audit_preserved.why_before_G1: once A1 membership is visible, choosing which lead rule wins could be influenced by which RDGs it affects; resolving it blind requires doing so before G1
prior_audit_preserved.proposed_resolution_not_applied: Freeze 1.2.1 (prospective): state which rule is authoritative. Recommended: the text rule — drop leads whose host fails a1_frame.key_host validation, apply RFC 3986 dot-segment removal and Freeze-1.1 percent normalisation — implemented as a new frozen lead normaliser; R17 re-registered against it.
